name: Narrowneck Reef (Gold Coast Reef)
shape_type_notes: Dual-arm split-V / chevron: two separate wishbone-shaped reef units ('north arm' and 'south arm' in this report's own labelling) set side by side alongshore, joined by a narrow central channel across which a small submerged weir (two containers) was added in 2004. Confirmed by text and four plan-view figures in the primary monitoring paper (Jackson et al. 2012, [R4]). This is NOT an inshore/offshore concentric-lobe arrangement (see gemini_comparison).
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north -- the Narrowneck isthmus trends roughly N-S per general regional geography, no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0.
polygon_components_notes: polygons_m[0] = north arm (x>0), polygons_m[1] = south arm (x<0, mirror image of the north arm in x). Both closed and non-self-intersecting (checked with shapely: is_valid=True, is_simple=True for both). No solid polygon is given for the central channel/waist (x approx -50 to 50) since it is open water crossed only by a small 2-container weir added in 2004, not a filled structure -- see md derivation/'Polygon construction'.
bbox_alt_note: A second source [R8] gives a conflicting 450 m (long) x 250 m (wide) for this same reef; not reconciled with the 600x350 [R9] figure used for this file's bounding box and polygon scaffold. Both are retained per the project reference rule.
area_m2_notes: Net area of the two schematic arm polygons above (shoelace formula: 57,475 m^2 each), NOT a published or surveyed figure -- it is a geometric consequence of this report's own illustrative vertex placement (see md 'Polygon construction'). Gross bounding-box area (600x350) = 210,000 m^2. Not directly comparable to Gemini's gross (75,000) or net (42,650) figures since Gemini's underlying shape (inshore/offshore lobes) differs from the alongshore-split shape used here.

crest_depth_m.datum: below low tide waterline (approx. LAT), as stated in sources -- design/2012 value

crest_depth_alt_note: Crest depth is time-varying and this single value should not be used without noting its date: as designed/1999 and as of the 2012 primary-source survey, crest was 'about 1-1.5m below low tide' [R4 p.13, also R2][R3]; by 2017, before the 2018 renewal, it had settled to 2.5-2.6 m below low tide [R2]; the 2018 renewal added 84 containers to raise the crest again but no source gives a specific post-renewal number.

distance_offshore_m.measured_from: shoreline -- treated as the reef's shoreward/inner edge; no source specifies exactly which point 'X m offshore' is measured to

orientation_notes: Two arms (north/south) run alongshore either side of a central channel/weir, matching the card's pre-existing 'split V shape... paddling channel between the arms' language [R3][R9]. The reef is understood to face the Gold Coast's predominant E-ESE swell (general regional geography, open east-facing coast), consistent with (though not independently confirmed to the same precision as) Gemini's claimed 090-120 deg incident swell direction -- no source found by either this report or Gemini states a precise degree figure. Alongshore axis 'north' is this report's own convention, not a sourced compass bearing.
materials: Sand-filled non-woven geotextile containers ('mega sandbags'), approx. 450 placed by 1999-2006 (arithmetic per [R4] p.3/Fig.4: ~408 from the original 1999-2000 construction + top-up, plus 42 in three later maintenance campaigns 2002-2006 [Fig.4 table: 10+15+17=42] = 450 total; R9 separately and independently gives a rounded 'more than 400' for the original build, consistent with ~408 but not an exact match to a card-invented '400') + 84 more added June 2018 [R9][R14]; each container approx. 20 m long, 3.0-4.8 m diameter [R1/R9 exact figure; corrected this pass from an earlier '3-4.5 m' rounding].

agree: general shape family (dual-arm chevron with 2 polygon components)
qualitative orientation (facing incoming E-ESE swell) -- precise degrees unverified by either party

disagree.gemini: Inshore Lobe + Offshore Lobe stacked cross-shore (same alongshore position, different offshore distances)
disagree.ours: North arm + South arm split alongshore (same offshore-distance range, different alongshore positions), joined by a central channel/weir
disagree.why_ours: The primary monitoring paper (Jackson et al. 2012, [R4]) explicitly states a weir was built 'between the two arms of the reef' and shows this in 4 separate plan-view figures (Figs. 2,4,5,7), consistently depicting two side-by-side wishbone lobes joined by a narrow waist -- not a near-shore ring and a further-offshore ring. This directly matches the card's own pre-existing 'split V shape... paddling channel between the arms' language [R3][R9]. Gemini's own audit already senses something is off (it flags the '180m offshore' label as ambiguous) but never revisits the underlying inshore/offshore-lobe topology itself, which this report identifies as the actual root issue.

Gemini's clean 400x220 matches neither of our two sourced figures and no citation ties it to a specific page in Gemini's own 3 listed sources; this report could not find '400' or '220' stated anywhere in the primary paper obtained, nor on the ICM webpage (re-checked, no plan dimensions present).

disagree.gemini: 75000 gross / 42650 net (internally inconsistent per Gemini's own audit)
disagree.ours: 210000 gross (600x350) / ~114950 net (this report's own schematic polygon)
disagree.why_ours: Gemini's own audit already flags its gross/net inconsistency without resolving it; our figures come from a different (alongshore-split) shape and are not directly comparable to Gemini's.

disagree.ours: 1.0-1.5 (2012 design value, R4) or 2.5-2.6 (2017 settled value, R2) depending on date
disagree.why_ours: No source found supports exactly 2.2 m. The primary paper states 1.0-1.5m as of 2012 [R4 p.13]; [R2] separately gives 2.5-2.6m for the settled, pre-2018-renewal (2017) state. 2.2 sits between these but is not derivable from either without an unstated averaging assumption; Gemini's own audit note cites three different numbers (-1.0m design, -2.5m settled, -1.5m post-2018-refurbishment), none of which is 2.2m either.

disagree.ours: 200 (single figure, treated as the shoreward edge of the whole two-arm structure)
disagree.why_ours: Gemini's tiered offshore-distance framing is a direct consequence of the rejected inshore/offshore-lobe topology. With the alongshore-split topology used here, there is no separate 'outer ridge' 300-380m out; the reef's full cross-shore extent (200-550m in this report's schematic) comes from each arm's own outer horn, not a second, more-offshore reef ring.

open_issues: No plan-view figure with a legible printed scale bar was found for this reef in any source consulted (primary paper, ICM webpage, or the card's image list); the polygon vertices in this file are a documented schematic, not a survey-grade digitization.
The card's own pre-existing footprint disagreement (350x600m [R9] vs. 450x250m [R8]) remains unreconciled; no third, tie-breaking source was found.

This report assumes north/south mirror symmetry between the two arms for the schematic polygon; Jackson et al. 2012 Fig. 4 suggests the two arms may not be perfectly identical, but source resolution does not support characterizing the actual asymmetry.

The exact shoreline azimuth at Narrowneck (to convert 'alongshore = positive north' into a true compass bearing) was not found in any source consulted; the isthmus's roughly N-S trend is inferred from general regional geography, not a stated figure.

Crest depth is genuinely time-varying (~1.0-1.5m as designed/2012 -> ~2.5-2.6m by 2017 settled -> an unstated, presumably shallower figure after the 2018 renewal); any single crest-depth number used elsewhere for this reef should specify which date/state it refers to.
The central channel's width (~100m, used to space the two arms in the schematic polygon) is this report's own unsourced assumption, not a published figure.
